There are large investors in a small market when it comes to cryptocurrency (small relative to something like forex, of course), and so there are individual organizations/investors which can have a huge effect on price, if they so choose. And a ton of the people in btc right now are people in the general public who bought into the internet hype, and so are not disciplined and experienced traders who know how to avoid the emotional reactions to volitility that put the whole market at risk. And people more interested in the tech/security side of crypto are seeing interesting innovations coming out of a lot of newcomers to the crypto market. The crash is coming, and it's coming hard.

Not a bad idea in theory. However, the problem is this -

The crypto market is so unstable, that there is no real way to tell when btc is going to crash until it is already in freefall. I have better places to put my limited funds that I know will show returns in the near future, and frankly don't have the funds to do this significantly unless it is done on margin. If I could find a good broker where I could do this on margin and put any significant amount into shorting btc, and then it goes up to $20k, I'm going to blow out my account well before I can make significant money off of it. And if I am trying to short it when it starts dropping significantly, the spreads on it will likely be large, and as volatile as it is it may go up significantly again before bottoming out. I'm not into the get-rich-quick type of trading, so I simply don't do markets with crazy levels of volatility unless I am absolutely sure of where it is going in the short-term.

But the problem is not just mine individually. The general public that is not that familiar with trading are not likely to have a solid grasp of when to short it. If it's made a bunch of gains recently and you've invested heavily in it (both financially and emotionally), it's hard to give up on it when it dips down toward your entry price. Especially if you've seen it go below and then come back up again. There's going to be a bunch of people who don't know what to do when the market comes down significantly, bought in too high and wait to sell until it's already in freefall to try recouping some of their losses, and that's just going to exacerbate the crash. Plenty of people have, and are going to make money on bitcoin. I think a lot of people are going to lose a whole lot of money on bitcoin. The lucky people are going to be the ones who know (or guess) the right time to get out of it.

Trading and investing are not gambling, if done well, imo. A better long-term strategy is to play safer markets with strategies that consistently make money over time. But I'm certainly no expert - I make most of my income from a 9-to-5 - so who knows?
